source.text: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ· Ἀνένδεκτόν ἐστιν τοῦ τὰ σκάνδαλα μὴ ἐλθεῖν, πλὴν οὐαὶ δι’ οὗ ἔρχεται·

records.literal_gloss: He said then to the disciples of him, Impossible it is for the stumbling blocks not to come, but woe [to him] through whom they come;

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "It is impossible for stumbling blocks not to come, but woe [to the one] through whom they come!
en.B: Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "Things that trip people up and lead them into sin will certainly come. But how terrible for the one who brings them!
en.R: Jesus said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "There will always be things that make people fall into sin. But how terrible it will be for the person who causes them!

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Il est impossible que les pierres d’achoppement n’arrivent pas, mais malheur [à celui] par qui elles arrivent !
fr.B: Jésus dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Il arrivera forcément des choses qui font trébucher les gens et les entraînent dans le péché. Mais malheur à celui par qui elles arrivent !
fr.R: Jésus a dit à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples : « Il y aura toujours des choses qui font tomber les gens dans le péché. Mais ce sera terrible pour celui qui en est la cause !

decisions.choice: stumbling blocks: things that make someone fall into sin or give up faith
decisions.reason: The word first meant the trigger of a trap, then anything that makes a person trip. In the Gospels it means something that leads a person into sin or away from God (7:23). The next verse shows that the danger is to "these little ones".

decisions.choice: it is impossible for them not to come: they are certain to come
decisions.reason: The phrase says the thing cannot be avoided. In a world like this one, people will be led into sin; the warning is for whoever does the leading.

decisions.choice: woe: a cry of grief and warning over someone headed for judgment
decisions.reason: As in 6:24-26 and 11:42-52, the word mourns and warns at once.

decisions.choice: woe (L); how terrible (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in 6:24-26 and 11:42: Literal keeps "woe"; Balanced and Readable use an everyday expression of grief and warning.

decisions.choice: things that trip people up and lead them into sin (B); things that make people fall into sin (R)
decisions.reason: "Stumbling block" is church language. Balanced keeps the picture of tripping and says where it leads; Readable gives the sense.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 17:4
alternatives: a separate quotation for each verse
decisions.reason: Jesus' words in 17:1-4 are one saying; the apostles speak in 17:5.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); historic presents kept as presents at Literal (17:37)
decisions.reason: As in Luke 2 and 4: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; the passé composé is how French is spoken and how young readers meet stories, so Readable uses it throughout. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, including the days of Noah and of Lot that Jesus recalls in 17:26-29. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: malheur à celui (L, B); ce sera terrible pour celui (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide keeps the traditional cry "malheur" at Literal and Balanced, where it is still current French for a warning of judgment (m3); Readable follows the English "how terrible". The generic "celui par qui" needs no gender setting.

source.text: λυσιτελεῖ αὐτῷ εἰ λίθος μυλικὸς περίκειται περὶ τὸν τράχηλον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἔρριπται εἰς τὴν θάλασσαν ἢ ἵνα σκανδαλίσῃ τῶν μικρῶν τούτων ἕνα.

records.literal_gloss: It is better for him if a stone of a mill is hung around the neck of him and he is thrown into the sea than that he should cause to stumble of these little ones one.

en.L: It is better for {{gender:that person|him}} if a millstone is hung around {{gender:their|his}} neck and {{gender:they are|he is}} thrown into the sea, than that {{gender:they|he}} should cause one of these little ones to stumble.
en.B: It would be better for {{gender:that person|him}} to be thrown into the sea with a millstone tied around {{gender:their|his}} neck than to make one of these little ones stumble.
en.R: It would be better for {{gender:that person|him}} to have a heavy stone tied around {{gender:their|his}} neck and be thrown into the sea. That would be better than causing one of these little ones to sin.

fr.L: Il vaut mieux pour lui qu’une meule de moulin soit placée autour de son cou et qu’il soit jeté dans la mer, plutôt qu’il fasse trébucher un seul de ces petits.
fr.B: Il vaudrait mieux pour lui être jeté dans la mer avec une meule attachée au cou que de faire trébucher un seul de ces petits.
fr.R: Il vaudrait mieux pour lui qu’on lui attache une grosse pierre autour du cou et qu’on le jette dans la mer. Ce serait mieux que de faire tomber dans le péché un de ces petits.

decisions.choice: a millstone: a heavy round stone for grinding grain
decisions.reason: The word means a stone of a mill. A person tied to it would sink and never come up. The picture is of a death without hope of rescue.

decisions.choice: these little ones: disciples who are weak or of little account
decisions.reason: Jesus is speaking to his disciples (17:1). The phrase points to followers who are humble and easily hurt, whom God cares for (compare 10:21; 12:32). It may include children, but is not limited to them.

decisions.choice: cause to stumble: lead into sin or away from faith
decisions.reason: The verb is formed from the word for stumbling blocks in 17:1.

decisions.choice: a heavy stone
decisions.reason: Readable describes the stone instead of naming it, since few readers have seen a millstone.

decisions.choice: be thrown into the sea with a millstone tied around their neck (B)
alternatives: if a millstone is hung around their neck and they are thrown into the sea
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the simpler English order with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: lui, son cou, il with no gender span
decisions.reason: The pronouns refer back to the generic "celui par qui" of 17:1, and French "son" does not mark the owner's sex, so French needs no setting where the English has "that person / their". The same holds for "ses affaires" (17:31) and "sa vie" (17:33).

source.text: προσέχετε ἑαυτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: Take heed to yourselves.

en.L: Watch yourselves.
en.B: Be on your guard.
en.R: So be careful how you act.

fr.L: Prenez garde à vous-mêmes.
fr.B: Soyez sur vos gardes.
fr.R: Alors, faites attention à votre façon d’agir.

decisions.choice: watch yourselves: looks both back to 17:1-2 and on to 17:3b-4
alternatives: only a warning about causing others to stumble
only an introduction to the teaching on forgiveness
decisions.reason: The words stand between the warning about causing others to sin and the teaching about a brother who sins. The disciples must watch that they do not lead others astray, and also how they treat those who wrong them.

decisions.choice: So be careful how you act.
decisions.reason: Readable says what the disciples are to watch.

source.text: ἐὰν ἁμάρτῃ ὁ ἀδελφός σου ἐπιτίμησον αὐτῷ, καὶ ἐὰν μετανοήσῃ ἄφες αὐτῷ·

records.literal_gloss: If should sin the brother of you, rebuke him, and if he should repent, forgive him;

en.L: If your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} sins, rebuke {{gender:them|him}}, and if {{gender:they repent|he repents}}, forgive {{gender:them|him}}.
en.B: When your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} does wrong, warn {{gender:them|him}}. Then if {{gender:they repent|he repents}}, forgive {{gender:them|him}}.
en.R: If your {{gender:brother or sister|brother}} sins, tell {{gender:them|him}} it is wrong. If {{gender:they turn|he turns}} away from the sin, forgive {{gender:them|him}}.

fr.L: Si {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}} pèche, adresse-lui des reproches, et s’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} se repent, pardonne-lui.
fr.B: Quand {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}} commet une faute, parle-lui franchement. Puis, s’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} se repent, pardonne-lui.
fr.R: Si {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}} pèche, dis-lui que c’est mal. S’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} se détourne de son péché, pardonne-lui.

decisions.choice: brother: a fellow member of God's people, man or woman
decisions.reason: As in 6:41-42, the word is used of anyone in the same community of faith.

decisions.choice: rebuke: tell plainly that what was done is wrong
decisions.reason: The verb means to speak firmly against something. The aim is that the one who sinned will turn back, as the next words show.

decisions.choice: repent: turn away from the wrong and change one's mind about it
decisions.reason: The verb is the one John and Jesus use for turning from sin to God (3:3; 5:32).

decisions.choice: if your brother sins: without "against you"
alternatives: if your brother sins against you
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add "against you", perhaps from 17:4 or Matthew 18:15. Early witnesses such as Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus lack it, and the SBLGNT follows them. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: warn (B); tell them it is wrong (R)
decisions.reason: "Rebuke" can sound like an angry scolding. Balanced and Readable give the sense of speaking plainly to win the person back.

decisions.choice: turn away from the sin
decisions.reason: As in 3:3 and 5:32, Readable explains what repenting is.

decisions.choice: {{gender:ton frère ou ta sœur|ton frère}}, then {{gender:il ou elle|il}} for the subject; "lui" with no span
decisions.reason: The brother is any fellow believer, man or woman (m1). The subject pronoun that agrees with the noun goes under the same setting, as the style guide asks; the object pronoun "lui" serves either sex, so Literal says "adresse-lui des reproches" rather than "reprends-le" and needs no span there. The same pattern carries into 17:4.

decisions.choice: se repentir (L, B); se détourner de son péché (R)
decisions.reason: The style guide's term for the New Testament; Readable explains it as the English Readable does ("turn away from the sin").

source.text: καὶ ἐὰν ἑπτάκις τῆς ἡμέρας ἁμαρτήσῃ εἰς σὲ καὶ ἑπτάκις ἐπιστρέψῃ πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Μετανοῶ, ἀφήσεις αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And if seven times in the day he should sin against you and seven times should return to you saying, I repent, you shall forgive him.

en.L: And if seven times in the day {{gender:they sin|he sins}} against you, and seven times {{gender:they return|he returns}} to you, saying, 'I repent,' you shall forgive {{gender:them|him}}."
en.B: Seven times in one day {{gender:they may|he may}} wrong you, and seven times come back and say, 'I repent.' Even so, forgive {{gender:them|him}}."
en.R: Maybe {{gender:they will|he will}} sin against you seven times in one day. And seven times {{gender:they will|he will}} come back to you and say, 'I am sorry. I will change.' You must still forgive {{gender:them|him}} each time."

fr.L: Et si sept fois dans la journée {{gender:il ou elle|il}} pèche contre toi, et que sept fois {{gender:il ou elle|il}} revienne vers toi en disant : “Je me repens”, tu lui pardonneras. »
fr.B: Même s’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} te fait du tort sept fois dans la même journée, et revient sept fois te dire : “Je me repens”, pardonne-lui. »
fr.R: Peut-être qu’{{gender:il ou elle|il}} péchera contre toi sept fois dans la même journée. Et sept fois, {{gender:il ou elle|il}} reviendra te dire : “Je regrette. Je vais changer.” Tu dois quand même lui pardonner chaque fois. »

decisions.choice: seven times: again and again, as often as it happens
alternatives: exactly seven times and no more
decisions.reason: Seven is the number of completeness in Scripture. Jesus does not set a limit; he says forgiveness must keep pace with repentance (compare Matthew 18:21-22).

decisions.choice: you shall forgive: a command
alternatives: a prediction that you will forgive
decisions.reason: The future tense here gives an order, as it does in the commandments.

decisions.choice: I repent: the words the person says on returning
decisions.reason: Jesus does not ask the disciple to judge whether the words are sincere. The words are enough.

decisions.choice: I am sorry. I will change. ... each time
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "I repent" means and makes the point of the repetition plain.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The apostles speak in 17:5.

source.text: Καὶ εἶπαν οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῷ κυρίῳ· Πρόσθες ἡμῖν πίστιν.

records.literal_gloss: And said the apostles to the Lord, Add to us faith.

en.L: And the apostles said to the Lord, "Add faith to us!"
en.B: The apostles said to the Lord, "Give us more faith!"
en.R: The apostles said to the Lord Jesus, "Make our faith stronger!"

fr.L: Et les apôtres dirent au Seigneur : « Ajoute-nous de la foi ! »
fr.B: Les apôtres dirent au Seigneur : « Donne-nous plus de foi ! »
fr.R: Les apôtres ont dit au Seigneur Jésus : « Rends notre foi plus forte ! »

decisions.choice: add: give more of
alternatives: give faith for the first time
decisions.reason: The verb means to add to what is already there. The apostles have faith, but feel it is too little for what Jesus has just asked of them.

decisions.choice: the Lord: Luke the narrator calls Jesus by his title
alternatives: a polite form of address only
decisions.reason: Luke often calls Jesus "the Lord" in his story (7:13; 10:1; 12:42).

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name, as in 12:42.

source.text: εἶπεν δὲ ὁ κύριος· Εἰ ἔχετε πίστιν ὡς κόκκον σινάπεως, ἐλέγετε ἂν τῇ συκαμίνῳ ταύτῃ· Ἐκριζώθητι καὶ φυτεύθητι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ· καὶ ὑπήκουσεν ἂν ὑμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: Said then the Lord, If you have faith like a grain of mustard, you would have said to the mulberry tree this, Be uprooted and be planted in the sea; and it would have obeyed you.

en.L: And the Lord said, "If you had faith like a grain of mustard, you would say to this mulberry tree, 'Be uprooted and be planted in the sea,' and it would obey you.
en.B: The Lord answered, "If you had faith the size of a mustard seed, you could tell this mulberry tree, 'Tear yourself up by the roots and be planted in the sea,' and it would do as you say.
en.R: The Lord answered, "Even if your faith were only as big as a tiny mustard seed, you could say to this tree, 'Pull your roots out of the ground and go plant yourself in the sea!' And the tree would obey you.

fr.L: Et le Seigneur dit : « Si vous aviez de la foi comme un grain de moutarde, vous diriez à ce mûrier : “Sois déraciné et sois planté dans la mer”, et il vous obéirait.
fr.B: Le Seigneur répondit : « Si vous aviez de la foi gros comme une graine de moutarde, vous pourriez dire à ce mûrier : “Arrache-toi avec tes racines et va te planter dans la mer”, et il ferait ce que vous dites.
fr.R: Le Seigneur a répondu : « Même si votre foi était aussi petite qu’une minuscule graine de moutarde, vous pourriez dire à cet arbre : “Arrache tes racines du sol et va te planter dans la mer !” Et l’arbre vous obéirait.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in God
decisions.reason: The point is not how much faith a person has, but that faith trusts God, for whom nothing is impossible (1:37).

decisions.choice: a grain of mustard: the mustard seed, known for being tiny
decisions.reason: The mustard seed was the smallest seed a farmer sowed (13:19). Even the smallest true faith is enough.

decisions.choice: mulberry tree: the black mulberry, a tree with deep, strong roots
decisions.reason: Luke uses a different word for the sycamore-fig that Zacchaeus climbs. This tree was known for roots that were hard to pull up.

decisions.choice: if you had faith: a condition that does not match the facts as they are
alternatives: if you have faith, as you do
decisions.reason: The verb in the "if" part is present, but the rest is put as something that would happen. Jesus implies that the apostles' faith is not even that small seed; the question is not how much faith, but whether it is real trust.

decisions.choice: be uprooted and planted in the sea: doing what seems impossible
alternatives: a promise of literal miracles with trees
decisions.reason: A tree planted in the sea is a deliberately impossible picture, to show what God can do through those who trust him.

decisions.choice: this tree
decisions.reason: Readable does not name the kind of tree; the meaning decision explains it.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 17:10
decisions.reason: Jesus' answer to the apostles runs on without a break.

source.text: Τίς δὲ ἐξ ὑμῶν δοῦλον ἔχων ἀροτριῶντα ἢ ποιμαίνοντα, ὃς εἰσελθόντι ἐκ τοῦ ἀγροῦ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ· Εὐθέως παρελθὼν ἀνάπεσε, ἀλλ’ οὐχὶ ἐρεῖ αὐτῷ· Ἑτοίμασον τί δειπνήσω καὶ περιζωσάμενος διακόνει μοι ἕως φάγω καὶ πίω, καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα φάγεσαι καὶ πίεσαι σύ;

records.literal_gloss: Which now of you having a slave plowing or shepherding, who having come in out of the field will say to him, Immediately having come recline? \v 8 But not will he say to him, Prepare what I may eat, and having girded yourself serve me while I eat and drink, and after these things will eat and drink you?

en.L: Which of you, having a slave plowing or tending sheep, will say to him when he has come in from the field, 'Come at once and recline [at table]'? \v 8 But will he not say to him, 'Prepare something for me to eat, and get dressed and serve me while I eat and drink, and after that you will eat and drink'?
en.B: Imagine that one of you has a servant who has been out plowing or tending the sheep. When he comes in from the field, will you tell him, 'Come straight in and take your place at the table'? \v 8 Will you not tell him instead, 'Make me something to eat. Then tie on your apron and serve me while I have my meal. You can eat and drink afterward'?
en.R: Let us say one of you has a servant who works out in the field, plowing or caring for sheep. When the servant comes in from work, you do not say to him, 'Come and sit down to eat right now.' \v 8 Instead, you say, 'Get my dinner ready. Put on your work clothes and serve me while I eat and drink. After that you can have your own meal.'

fr.L: Qui d’entre vous, ayant un esclave qui laboure ou qui garde les troupeaux, lui dira quand il rentre des champs : “Viens vite t’étendre [à table]” ? \v 8 Ne lui dira-t-il pas plutôt : “Prépare-moi de quoi dîner, ceins-toi et sers-moi pendant que je mange et que je bois ; et après cela, toi, tu mangeras et tu boiras” ?
fr.B: Imaginez que l’un de vous ait un serviteur qui laboure ou qui garde les moutons. Quand il revient des champs, lui direz-vous : “Viens vite prendre place à table” ? \v 8 Ne lui direz-vous pas plutôt : “Prépare-moi à manger. Puis mets ton tablier et sers-moi pendant que je prends mon repas. Tu mangeras et tu boiras ensuite” ?
fr.R: Supposons que l’un de vous ait un serviteur qui travaille dehors, dans les champs : il laboure ou il s’occupe des moutons. Quand le serviteur rentre du travail, vous ne lui dites pas : “Viens tout de suite t’asseoir pour manger.” \v 8 Au contraire, vous lui dites : “Prépare mon dîner. Mets tes vêtements de travail et sers-moi pendant que je mange et que je bois. Après, tu pourras prendre ton propre repas.”

decisions.choice: slave: a person owned by a master and at his command
decisions.reason: The word is the ordinary word for a slave (12:37). A small farmer might own one slave who did the field work and the housework too.

decisions.choice: two questions that expect the answers "no" and "yes"
decisions.reason: The first question expects "No, no one would say that"; the second expects "Yes, of course he would". Jesus draws on what everyone knew about masters and slaves.

decisions.choice: recline: lie on a couch at a meal
decisions.reason: At a meal people lay on their side around a low table. To tell a slave to recline would be to treat him as a guest.

decisions.choice: having girded yourself: tying up one's long robe to be ready for work
alternatives: putting on a belt for decoration
decisions.reason: A long robe was tucked up into the belt for work or serving (12:35, 37).

decisions.choice: Imagine that one of you (B); Let us say one of you (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable set up the picture first, then ask (B) or state (R) what the master does.

decisions.choice: statements instead of questions
decisions.reason: Readable gives the expected answers as plain statements.

decisions.choice: take your place at the table; tie on your apron (B); sit down to eat; put on your work clothes (R)
decisions.reason: Modern readers sit at meals and do not tuck up robes; the meaning decisions explain the customs.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m1) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave". Balanced says "has a servant" rather than "owns".

decisions.choice: un esclave (L); un serviteur (B, R)
decisions.reason: As the style guide and the English: Literal keeps that the man was owned (m1), Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", the word for one who works at a master's command. The same in 17:9-10.

decisions.choice: t’étendre [à table]; ceins-toi (L)
alternatives: mets-toi à table; attache ta ceinture
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the customs the meaning decisions explain: guests lay on couches at a meal (m3), and a servant tucked up his robe with a belt before working (m4). "Ceindre" is old but is the French word for that act; Balanced and Readable use today's pictures ("prendre place à table", "mets ton tablier").

source.text: μὴ ἔχει χάριν τῷ δούλῳ ὅτι ἐποίησεν τὰ διαταχθέντα;

records.literal_gloss: Not does he have thanks to the slave because he did the things having been commanded?

en.L: He does not have thanks for the slave because he did the things commanded, does he?
en.B: The master does not owe the servant any thanks for doing what he was ordered to do, does he?
en.R: The master does not thank the servant for doing what he was told to do.

fr.L: A-t-il de la reconnaissance pour l’esclave parce qu’il a fait ce qui avait été ordonné ?
fr.B: Le maître ne doit pas de remerciements au serviteur parce qu’il a fait ce qu’on lui avait commandé, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Le maître ne remercie pas le serviteur d’avoir fait ce qu’on lui avait demandé.

decisions.choice: thanks: gratitude owed to someone
decisions.reason: The noun usually translated "grace" also means thanks. With the verb "have" it is the usual way to say "be grateful" (1 Timothy 1:12). Here it is thanks, not God's grace.

decisions.choice: slave
decisions.reason: As in 17:7.

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "no"
decisions.reason: The form of the question expects "No, he does not".

decisions.choice: a statement instead of a question
decisions.reason: Readable gives the expected answer as a plain statement.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: οὕτως καὶ ὑμεῖς, ὅταν ποιήσητε πάντα τὰ διαταχθέντα ὑμῖν, λέγετε ὅτι Δοῦλοι ἀχρεῖοί ἐσμεν, ὃ ὠφείλομεν ποιῆσαι πεποιήκαμεν.

records.literal_gloss: Thus also you, when you may have done all the things having been commanded you, say, Slaves unworthy are we; that which we were bound to do we have done.

en.L: So also you, when you have done all the things commanded you, say, 'We are unworthy slaves; what we were obligated to do, we have done.'"
en.B: It is the same with you. When you have done everything you were ordered to do, say, 'We are unworthy servants. We have done no more than we were bound to do.'"
en.R: It is the same with you. When you have done all that you were told to do, you should say, 'We are only servants, and we have earned nothing special. We have just done the work we were supposed to do.'"

fr.L: Ainsi vous aussi, quand vous aurez fait tout ce qui vous a été ordonné, dites : “Nous sommes des esclaves sans mérite ; ce que nous devions faire, nous l’avons fait.” »
fr.B: Il en va de même pour vous. Quand vous aurez fait tout ce qui vous a été ordonné, dites : “Nous sommes des serviteurs sans mérite. Nous n’avons fait que ce que nous devions faire.” »
fr.R: C’est la même chose pour vous. Quand vous avez fait tout ce qu’on vous a demandé, vous devez dire : “Nous sommes seulement des serviteurs, et nous n’avons rien gagné de spécial. Nous avons juste fait le travail que nous devions faire.” »

decisions.choice: unworthy: having no special claim, owed nothing extra
decisions.reason: The word can mean useless (Matthew 25:30), but these slaves have done all they were told. Here it means they have earned no reward of their own; they have only done their duty. Any reward is the master's gift (compare 12:37).

decisions.choice: slaves: those who belong to their master
decisions.reason: The disciples stand before God as slaves before their master: all they do is already owed to him.

decisions.choice: what we were obligated to do: obedience is owed, not a favor done to God
alternatives: a statement that obedience does not matter
decisions.reason: The parable does not make obedience small. It answers the request for more faith (17:5): faith simply does what the Master asks, without claiming credit.

decisions.choice: only servants, and we have earned nothing special
decisions.reason: "Unworthy" can sound like "worthless". Readable gives the sense the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: Jesus' answer, begun at 17:6, ends here.

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: sans mérite (L, B)
decisions.reason: The word means having no special claim, owed nothing extra (m1). "Inutiles", the traditional French, says that the servants are of no use, which the parable does not say; "indignes" sounds like shame. "Sans mérite" says that they have earned nothing beyond their duty.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ πορεύεσθαι εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ αὐτὸς διήρχετο διὰ μέσον Σαμαρείας καὶ Γαλιλαίας.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the going to Jerusalem that he was passing through [the] midst of Samaria and Galilee.

en.L: And it happened, while going to Jerusalem, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was passing through the middle of Samaria and Galilee.
en.B: As Jesus made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} way toward Jerusalem, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went through the region between Samaria and Galilee.
en.R: Jesus was still traveling toward Jerusalem. He went through the area where Samaria and Galilee meet.

fr.L: Et il arriva, en allant à Jérusalem, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passait par le milieu de la Samarie et de la Galilée.
fr.B: Tandis que Jésus faisait route vers Jérusalem, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} passa par la région située entre la Samarie et la Galilée.
fr.R: Jésus était toujours en route vers Jérusalem. Il est passé par la région où la Samarie et la Galilée se touchent.

decisions.choice: through the middle of Samaria and Galilee: along the region between the two
alternatives: through Samaria and then through Galilee
decisions.reason: The phrase is unusual. Galilee lay north of Samaria, and a traveler going toward Jerusalem would not pass through Samaria and then Galilee. The likely sense is that Jesus went along the border land between them, which suits a story with both a Samaritan and Jews in it.

decisions.choice: going to Jerusalem: the journey Jesus set out on at 9:51
decisions.reason: Luke reminds the reader that Jesus is on his way to Jerusalem, where he will suffer (9:51; 13:22).

decisions.choice: the region between (B); the area where Samaria and Galilee meet (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the likely sense, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: καὶ εἰσερχομένου αὐτοῦ εἴς τινα κώμην ἀπήντησαν δέκα λεπροὶ ἄνδρες, οἳ ἔστησαν πόρρωθεν, καὶ αὐτοὶ ἦραν φωνὴν λέγοντες· Ἰησοῦ ἐπιστάτα, ἐλέησον ἡμᾶς.

records.literal_gloss: And on the entering of him into a certain village met [him] ten leprous men, who stood afar off, \v 13 and they lifted up [their] voice saying, Jesus, Master, have mercy on us.

en.L: And as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered a certain village, ten leprous men met {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who stood far off; \v 13 and they lifted up [their] voice, saying, "Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!"
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came into a village, ten men with leprosy came toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They kept their distance \v 13 and called out loudly, "Jesus! Master! Have mercy on us!"
en.R: As Jesus was going into a village, ten men with a terrible skin disease came toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They stood far away from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \v 13 They shouted, "Jesus! Master! Please have mercy on us!"

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entrait dans un village, dix hommes lépreux vinrent à {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} rencontre ; ils s’arrêtèrent au loin \v 13 et ils élevèrent la voix en disant : « Jésus, Maître, aie pitié de nous ! »
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entrait dans un village, dix hommes atteints de la lèpre vinrent vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils restèrent à distance \v 13 et crièrent très fort : « Jésus ! Maître ! Aie pitié de nous ! »
fr.R: Au moment où Jésus entrait dans un village, dix hommes qui avaient une terrible maladie de peau sont venus vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils sont restés loin de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. \v 13 Ils ont crié : « Jésus ! Maître ! Aie pitié de nous, s’il {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} plaît ! »

decisions.choice: leprous: having a serious skin disease that made a person unclean under the law
alternatives: having the disease now called leprosy only
decisions.reason: As at 5:12. The law of Moses required such people to live apart and to warn others away (Leviticus 13:45-46).

decisions.choice: stood far off: kept the distance the law required
decisions.reason: Because of their disease they could not come near other people (Leviticus 13:46).

decisions.choice: Master: one with authority, who gives orders
decisions.reason: This is the disciples' word for Jesus in Luke (5:5; 8:24). Only here does someone outside the disciples use it.

decisions.choice: have mercy on us: take pity on us and help us
decisions.reason: The cry asks for help in need, as the blind man asks in 18:38.

decisions.choice: a terrible skin disease
decisions.reason: As at 5:12: "leprosy" now means one particular disease.

decisions.choice: called out loudly
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the Hebrew-sounding idiom.

decisions.choice: Maître at every level
decisions.reason: Luke's word is for one with authority who gives orders (m3). French "Maître" carries that sense and is the usual address to Jesus; "Chef" or "Patron" would sound like a workplace. French also says "Maître" for "Teacher" (18:18), so the two Greek words are not told apart in French.

decisions.choice: lépreux (L); atteints de la lèpre (B); une terrible maladie de peau (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: today "la lèpre" names one disease, while the word covered several serious skin diseases (m1), so Readable describes it.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἐπιδείξατε ἑαυτοὺς τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen [them] he said to them, Having gone show yourselves to the priests.

en.L: And having seen [them], {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Go, show yourselves to the priests."
en.B: Jesus saw them and told them, "Go and let the priests examine you."
en.R: When Jesus saw them, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Go and let the priests look at your skin."

fr.L: Et, [les] ayant vus, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Allez vous montrer aux prêtres. »
fr.B: Jésus les vit et leur dit : « Allez vous faire examiner par les prêtres. »
fr.R: Quand Jésus les a vus, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur a dit : « Allez montrer votre peau aux prêtres. »

decisions.choice: show yourselves to the priests: the step the law required before a cleansed person could return to the community
alternatives: a test of whether they were sick
decisions.reason: As at 5:14. A priest examined the skin and declared the person clean (Leviticus 14:1-32). Jesus sends them before they are healed, so going was an act of trust.

decisions.choice: let the priests examine you (B); let the priests look at your skin (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:14, Balanced and Readable say why they were to go.

source.text: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ὑπάγειν αὐτοὺς ἐκαθαρίσθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the going of them they were cleansed.

en.L: And it happened, as they went, [that] they were cleansed.
en.B: On their way there, they were made clean.
en.R: While they were going, they were healed and made clean.

fr.L: Et il arriva, pendant qu’ils s’en allaient, [qu’]ils furent purifiés.
fr.B: En chemin, ils furent rendus purs.
fr.R: Pendant qu’ils marchaient, ils ont été guéris, et ils sont devenus purs.

decisions.choice: were cleansed: healed of the disease, and so made clean under the law
decisions.reason: As at 5:12-13, healing and being made clean go together.

decisions.choice: were cleansed: by God
decisions.reason: The passive leaves the one who healed them unnamed; 17:15-18 shows that the healing came from God through Jesus.

decisions.choice: healed and made clean
decisions.reason: Readable says that being clean meant being healed.

source.text: εἷς δὲ ἐξ αὐτῶν, ἰδὼν ὅτι ἰάθη, ὑπέστρεψεν μετὰ φωνῆς μεγάλης δοξάζων τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον παρὰ τοὺς πόδας αὐτοῦ εὐχαριστῶν αὐτῷ· καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν Σαμαρίτης.

records.literal_gloss: One then of them, having seen that he was healed, turned back with a voice loud glorifying God, \v 16 and he fell on [his] face at the feet of him giving thanks to him; and he was a Samaritan.

en.L: And one of them, seeing that he was healed, turned back, glorifying God with a loud voice, \v 16 and he fell on [his] face at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} feet, giving thanks to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; and he was a Samaritan.
en.B: One of them, when he saw that he was healed, turned back, giving glory to God with a loud voice. \v 16 He fell face down at the feet of Jesus, thanking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. And the man was a Samaritan.
en.R: One of the men saw that he was healed. He came back, shouting and giving glory to God. \v 16 He bowed down at the feet of Jesus with his face to the ground and thanked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. This man was a Samaritan, not a Jew.

fr.L: Or l’un d’eux, voyant qu’il était guéri, revint sur ses pas, glorifiant Dieu d’une voix forte, \v 16 et il tomba sur [sa] face à {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} pieds, {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} rendant grâce ; et c’était un Samaritain.
fr.B: L’un d’eux, quand il vit qu’il était guéri, revint sur ses pas en rendant gloire à Dieu d’une voix forte. \v 16 Il se jeta face contre terre aux pieds de Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} remercia. Or cet homme était un Samaritain.
fr.R: L’un des hommes a vu qu’il était guéri. Il est revenu en criant et en rendant gloire à Dieu. \v 16 Il s’est prosterné aux pieds de Jésus, le visage contre le sol, et il {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a remercié. Cet homme était un Samaritain, il n’était pas juif.

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praising God for what he had done
decisions.reason: As in 5:25 and 7:16, the healed man honors God aloud for the healing.

decisions.choice: Samaritan: one of the people of Samaria, despised by many Jews
alternatives: a man from the city of Samaria only
decisions.reason: Jews and Samaritans had a long history of hostility over worship and descent (9:52-53; John 4:9). Like the Samaritan in Jesus' story (10:33), it is the outsider who does what is right.

decisions.choice: fell on his face: bowed with his face to the ground
decisions.reason: A gesture of deep honor and thanks (5:12).

decisions.choice: the feet of Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since "his" could refer to the man.

decisions.choice: not a Jew
decisions.reason: Readable adds what made this man different from the others, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ἀποκριθεὶς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν· Οὐχὶ οἱ δέκα ἐκαθαρίσθησαν;

records.literal_gloss: Having answered then Jesus said, Not the ten were cleansed?

en.L: And Jesus answered and said, "Were not the ten cleansed?
en.B: Jesus responded, "Ten men were made clean, were they not?
en.R: Jesus asked, "Did not all ten men become clean?

fr.L: Et Jésus, répondant, dit : « Les dix n’ont-ils pas été purifiés ?
fr.B: Jésus prit la parole : « Dix hommes ont été rendus purs, n’est-ce pas ?
fr.R: Jésus a demandé : « Les dix hommes ne sont-ils pas tous devenus purs ?

decisions.choice: a question expecting the answer "yes"
alternatives: a real question asking for information
decisions.reason: Jesus knows that all ten were cleansed. The question points to the one who came back.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 17:18
decisions.reason: Jesus' three questions are one speech.

source.text: οἱ δὲ ἐννέα ποῦ;

records.literal_gloss: But the nine, where?

en.L: But the nine, where [are they]?
en.B: So where are the other nine?
en.R: Where are the other nine men?

fr.L: Mais les neuf, où [sont-ils] ?
fr.B: Alors, où sont les neuf autres ?
fr.R: Où sont les neuf autres hommes ?

decisions.choice: where are the nine: an expression of disappointment
alternatives: a request for someone to find them
decisions.reason: Jesus does not want to know where they are; he grieves that they did not return.

decisions.choice: the other nine
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear which nine are meant.

source.text: οὐχ εὑρέθησαν ὑποστρέψαντες δοῦναι δόξαν τῷ θεῷ εἰ μὴ ὁ ἀλλογενὴς οὗτος;

records.literal_gloss: None was there found having returned to give glory to God except the foreigner this?

en.L: Was no one found who returned to give glory to God except this foreigner?"
en.B: Is this outsider the only one who came back to give glory to God?"
en.R: Did no one come back to give glory to God except this man from another people?"

fr.L: Ne s’en est-il trouvé aucun qui soit revenu donner gloire à Dieu, sinon cet étranger ? »
fr.B: Cet homme d’un autre peuple est-il le seul à être revenu rendre gloire à Dieu ? »
fr.R: Personne n’est revenu rendre gloire à Dieu, sauf cet homme qui vient d’un autre peuple ? »

decisions.choice: foreigner: one of another people, not of Israel
decisions.reason: The word means one of another race or nation. It was the word carved on the temple barrier warning foreigners not to go further into the courts. To a Jew a Samaritan was such an outsider.

decisions.choice: to give glory to God: honoring God as the one who healed
decisions.reason: The man glorified God (17:15) and thanked Jesus (17:16). Luke shows that to thank Jesus is to honor God, whose power was at work in him.

decisions.choice: Is this outsider the only one
alternatives: Was no one found ... except this foreigner
decisions.reason: Balanced turns the negative question round with the same meaning.

decisions.choice: outsider (B); man from another people (R)
decisions.reason: Both say that he did not belong to Israel; "foreigner" can suggest someone from far away.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀναστὰς πορεύου· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to him, Having risen up go forth; the faith of you has cured you.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Get up [and] go; your faith has saved you."
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told him, "Stand up and go on your way. Your faith has made you well."
en.R: Then Jesus said to him, "Get up and go on your way. Your faith has made you well and saved you."

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Lève-toi [et] va ; ta foi t’a sauvé. »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Relève-toi et va ton chemin. Ta foi t’a guéri. »
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus lui a dit : « Lève-toi et va ton chemin. Ta foi t’a guéri et sauvé. »

decisions.choice: has saved you: has made you well, and more than that, has rescued you
decisions.reason: The verb means to save or rescue, and in stories of healing to make well (8:48; 18:42). All ten were healed, but only to this man does Jesus say these words, after he came back to give thanks. The words used to the forgiven woman (7:50) suggest that he received more than healing.

decisions.choice: faith: his trust in Jesus, shown when he went and when he came back
decisions.reason: He set out for the priests before he was healed and returned to Jesus once he saw it.

decisions.choice: made you well (B); made you well and saved you (R)
decisions.reason: As in 8:48: Literal keeps "saved", Balanced says what happened to his body, and Readable uses both words so that neither sense is lost.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker.

source.text: Ἐπερωτηθεὶς δὲ ὑπὸ τῶν Φαρισαίων πότε ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἀπεκρίθη αὐτοῖς καὶ εἶπεν· Οὐκ ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ παρατηρήσεως, οὐδὲ ἐροῦσιν· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε ἤ· Ἐκεῖ· ἰδοὺ γὰρ ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ ἐντὸς ὑμῶν ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: Having been asked now by the Pharisees when is coming the kingdom of God, he answered them and said, Not comes the kingdom of God with careful observation, \v 21 nor will they say, Look here, or, There; look for the kingdom of God in the midst of you is.

en.L: And having been asked by the Pharisees when the kingdom of God is coming, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered them and said, "The kingdom of God is not coming with careful observation, \v 21 nor will they say, 'Look, here [it is]!' or 'There!' For look, the kingdom of God is in your midst."
en.B: Once the Pharisees asked Jesus when the kingdom of God would come. He answered them, "The kingdom of God does not come in a way you can watch for and track. \v 21 People will not say, 'It is here!' or 'It is over there!' For the kingdom of God is among you."
en.R: One day the Pharisees asked Jesus, "When will the kingdom of God come?" Jesus answered, "The kingdom of God does not come with signals you can watch for. \v 21 People will not say, 'Look, here it is!' or 'There it is!' The truth is, the kingdom of God is right here among you."

fr.L: Et, interrogé par les Pharisiens [pour savoir] quand vient le royaume de Dieu, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur répondit et dit : « Le royaume de Dieu ne vient pas avec une observation minutieuse, \v 21 et on ne dira pas : “Voici, [il est] ici !” ou : “Là !” Car voici, le royaume de Dieu est au milieu de vous. »
fr.B: Un jour, les Pharisiens demandèrent à Jésus quand viendrait le royaume de Dieu. Il leur répondit : « Le royaume de Dieu ne vient pas d’une manière qu’on puisse guetter et suivre des yeux. \v 21 On ne dira pas : “Il est ici !” ou : “Il est là-bas !” Car le royaume de Dieu est parmi vous. »
fr.R: Un jour, les Pharisiens ont demandé à Jésus : « Quand le royaume de Dieu va-t-il venir ? » Jésus a répondu : « Le royaume de Dieu ne vient pas avec des signaux qu’on peut guetter. \v 21 Les gens ne diront pas : “Regardez, il est ici !” ou : “Il est là !” La vérité, c’est que le royaume de Dieu est ici même, au milieu de vous. »

decisions.choice: the Pharisees: a Jewish movement devoted to keeping the law of Moses in every part of life
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 12:1. Many Jews of the time expected God to bring in his kingdom openly, with signs that could be read.

decisions.choice: careful observation: watching closely for signs, as one watches the sky
decisions.reason: The word is used for watching the stars or watching closely for something to happen. The kingdom does not arrive in a way that can be predicted by reading signs.

decisions.choice: in your midst: present among you, in the person and work of Jesus
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "inside you" or "among you". Jesus is speaking to Pharisees who opposed him, and elsewhere the kingdom is something people enter, not something inside them. The kingdom has come near in Jesus' own work (11:20). The reading "within you" is old and has long been held.

decisions.choice: for look: the reason the cries "here!" and "there!" miss the point
decisions.reason: The kingdom is not somewhere else to be pointed at; it is already present.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows; here it is also part of the cries people make. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: a direct question (R); a new sentence for the question (B)
decisions.reason: Readable puts the Pharisees' question in their own words.

decisions.choice: in a way you can watch for and track
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the phrase.

decisions.choice: The truth is ... right here
decisions.reason: Readable carries the force of "look" with words that point to what is present.

decisions.choice: les Pharisiens; le royaume de Dieu at every level
decisions.reason: The style guide's terms for the New Testament, as in Mark: the same words at every level, Readable included. "Le règne" would bring out God's rule but lose the picture of a kingdom that comes.

decisions.choice: au milieu de vous (L, R); parmi vous (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the kingdom as present among them in the person and work of Jesus (m3). "En vous" would make it an inner state of the Pharisees; both French phrases say presence in their midst.

source.text: Εἶπεν δὲ πρὸς τοὺς μαθητάς· Ἐλεύσονται ἡμέραι ὅτε ἐπιθυμήσετε μίαν τῶν ἡμερῶν τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἰδεῖν καὶ οὐκ ὄψεσθε.

records.literal_gloss: He said then to the disciples, Will come days when you will desire one of the days of the Son of Man to see, and not you will see [it].

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the disciples, "Days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see [it].
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the disciples, "There will be days when you ache to see even one day of the Son of Man, but you will not get to see it.
en.R: Then Jesus said to the disciples, "A time is coming when you will want very much to see just one day of the Son of Man. But you will not see it.

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit aux disciples : « Des jours viendront où vous désirerez voir un des jours du Fils de l’homme, et vous ne [le] verrez pas.
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit aux disciples : « Il viendra des jours où vous brûlerez de voir ne serait-ce qu’un seul jour du Fils de l’homme, mais vous ne le verrez pas.
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus a dit aux disciples : « Un temps va venir où vous aurez très envie de voir un seul jour du Fils de l’homme. Mais vous ne le verrez pas.

decisions.choice: one of the days of the Son of Man: a day of the Son of Man's presence
alternatives: the day of his return only
the days of Jesus' ministry looked back on
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean a day like those when Jesus was with them, or the first day of his coming in power. The disciples will long for him in hard times and will not yet see his coming.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus' name for himself
decisions.reason: Jesus calls himself by this name, drawn from Daniel 7:13-14 (5:24; 9:26).

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and runs to 17:35
decisions.reason: Jesus' words to the disciples in 17:22-35 are one speech.

decisions.choice: ache to see
decisions.reason: Balanced uses a word with the strength of the longing.

source.text: καὶ ἐροῦσιν ὑμῖν· Ἰδοὺ ἐκεῖ· Ἰδοὺ ὧδε· μὴ ἀπέλθητε μηδὲ διώξητε.

records.literal_gloss: And they will say to you, Look there, look here; not go forth nor follow.

en.L: And they will say to you, 'Look, there!' 'Look, here!' Do not go out, nor follow.
en.B: People will tell you, 'Look over there!' or 'Look here!' Do not go out, and do not run after them.
en.R: People will tell you, 'Look, over there!' or 'Look, right here!' Do not go out to see. Do not follow them.

fr.L: Et on vous dira : “Voici, [il est] là !” “Voici, [il est] ici !” N’y allez pas, et ne suivez pas.
fr.B: On vous dira : “Regardez là-bas !” ou : “Regardez ici !” N’y allez pas, et ne courez pas après eux.
fr.R: Les gens vous diront : “Regardez, là-bas !” ou : “Regardez, juste ici !” N’y allez pas pour voir. Ne les suivez pas.

decisions.choice: they will say: people in general
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; it means people will say.

decisions.choice: look, there! look, here!: claims that the Son of Man has come in some place
decisions.reason: The cries echo 17:21, but here they are claims about the Son of Man's coming, which will need no one to point it out (17:24).

decisions.choice: look
decisions.reason: Here the word is part of what people shout, so every level keeps it.

decisions.choice: run after them (B); follow them (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whom the disciples are not to follow.

source.text: ὥσπερ γὰρ ἡ ἀστραπὴ ἀστράπτουσα ἐκ τῆς ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν εἰς τὴν ὑπ’ οὐρανὸν λάμπει, οὕτως ἔσται ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐν τῇ ἡμέρᾳ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: As for the lightning flashing from the [one end] under the sky to the [other end] under the sky shines, thus will be the Son of Man in the day of him.

en.L: For as the lightning, flashing from one [end] under the sky, shines to the other [end] under the sky, so will the Son of Man be in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} day.
en.B: When lightning flashes, it lights up the sky from one edge to the other. That is how the Son of Man will be on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} day.
en.R: When lightning flashes, it lights up the whole sky from one side to the other. The day the Son of Man comes will be like that. Everyone will see it.

fr.L: Car, comme l’éclair, en jaillissant d’un [bout] sous le ciel, brille jusqu’à l’autre [bout] sous le ciel, ainsi sera le Fils de l’homme en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} jour.
fr.B: Quand l’éclair jaillit, il illumine le ciel d’un bout à l’autre. Ainsi en sera-t-il du Fils de l’homme en {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} jour.
fr.R: Quand il y a un éclair, il illumine tout le ciel d’un côté à l’autre. Ce sera comme cela le jour où le Fils de l’homme viendra. Tout le monde verra cela.

decisions.choice: lightning across the sky: sudden, and seen by everyone everywhere
decisions.reason: No one has to point out lightning; everyone sees it at once. So no one will need to say "here" or "there" (17:23).

decisions.choice: in his day: included
decisions.reason: Some early manuscripts, including Papyrus 75 and Codex Vaticanus, lack "in his day". Most manuscripts have it, and the SBLGNT includes it. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man in his day: his coming in glory
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the day when the Son of Man is revealed (17:30; 9:26).

decisions.choice: Everyone will see it.
decisions.reason: Readable says the point of the picture, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: two sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the picture first and the comparison second.

source.text: πρῶτον δὲ δεῖ αὐτὸν πολλὰ παθεῖν καὶ ἀποδοκιμασθῆναι ἀπὸ τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης.

records.literal_gloss: First however it behooves him many things to suffer and to be rejected by the generation this.

en.L: But first it is necessary for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to suffer many things and to be rejected by this generation.
en.B: But before that, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must go through great suffering and be turned away by the people of this generation.
en.R: But first {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} must suffer many things. The people living now will reject {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Mais d’abord il faut qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} souffre beaucoup et qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} soit rejeté par cette génération.
fr.B: Mais auparavant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} doit endurer de grandes souffrances et être rejeté par les gens de cette génération.
fr.R: Mais d’abord, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} doit beaucoup souffrir. Les gens d’aujourd’hui vont {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rejeter.

decisions.choice: it is necessary: it is part of God's plan
decisions.reason: The word is used for what must happen because God has willed it and Scripture has said it (9:22; 24:26).

decisions.choice: be rejected: be tested and turned away as worthless
decisions.reason: The verb is used of builders who reject a stone (20:17; Psalm 118:22).

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of Jesus' own time
decisions.reason: As in 7:31 and 11:29-32, the phrase means the people living then who refused Jesus.

decisions.choice: the people living now
decisions.reason: Readable explains the phrase.

source.text: καὶ καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Νῶε, οὕτως ἔσται καὶ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·

records.literal_gloss: And as it came to pass in the days of Noah, thus will it be also in the days of the Son of Man;

en.L: And just as it was in the days of Noah, so will it be also in the days of the Son of Man.
en.B: What happened in Noah's time will happen again in the days of the Son of Man.
en.R: When the Son of Man comes, it will be the same as it was in Noah's time.

fr.L: Et comme il en a été aux jours de Noé, ainsi en sera-t-il aussi aux jours du Fils de l’homme.
fr.B: Ce qui s’est passé au temps de Noé se passera de nouveau aux jours du Fils de l’homme.
fr.R: Quand le Fils de l’homme viendra, ce sera comme au temps de Noé.

decisions.choice: the days of Noah: the time before the flood
decisions.reason: Genesis 6-7 tells how God sent the flood on a world full of violence, and saved Noah and his family in the ark.

decisions.choice: the Son of Man first
decisions.reason: Readable starts with the subject of the comparison.

source.text: ἤσθιον, ἔπινον, ἐγάμουν, ἐγαμίζοντο, ἄχρι ἧς ἡμέρας εἰσῆλθεν Νῶε εἰς τὴν κιβωτόν, καὶ ἦλθεν ὁ κατακλυσμὸς καὶ ἀπώλεσεν πάντας.

records.literal_gloss: They were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage, until that day entered Noah into the ark, and came the flood and destroyed all.

en.L: They were eating, they were drinking, they were marrying, they were being given in marriage, until the day Noah entered into the ark, and the flood came and destroyed [them] all.
en.B: People were eating and drinking, taking wives and being given as wives, right up to the day Noah went into the ark. Then the flood came and wiped them all out.
en.R: People were eating and drinking and getting married, until the day Noah went into the big boat. Then the flood came and killed them all.

fr.L: Ils mangeaient, ils buvaient, ils épousaient, ils étaient donnés en mariage, jusqu’au jour où Noé est entré dans l’arche ; et le déluge est venu, et il les a tous fait périr.
fr.B: Les gens mangeaient et buvaient, les hommes prenaient femme et les femmes étaient données en mariage, jusqu’au jour où Noé est entré dans l’arche. Alors le déluge est venu et les a tous anéantis.
fr.R: Les gens mangeaient, buvaient et se mariaient, jusqu’au jour où Noé est entré dans le grand bateau. Alors le déluge est arrivé, et il les a tous tués.

decisions.choice: eating, drinking, marrying: ordinary life going on as usual
decisions.reason: None of these things is wrong. The point is that people went on as if nothing would happen, and were not ready.

decisions.choice: marrying, being given in marriage: men took wives, and fathers gave their daughters to be married
decisions.reason: Marriages were arranged by families; the bride was given by her father.

decisions.choice: Noah entered the ark, and the flood came
big boat
decisions.reason: Readable describes the ark for readers who do not know the word.

decisions.choice: imperfect and passé composé ("est entré", "est venu") at every level
alternatives: passé simple at Literal and Balanced
decisions.reason: These are Jesus's words, so the past events of Noah and Lot (17:26-29) are told in the tenses of speech, as the style guide asks for stories told inside speech.

source.text: ὁμοίως καθὼς ἐγένετο ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις Λώτ· ἤσθιον, ἔπινον, ἠγόραζον, ἐπώλουν, ἐφύτευον, ᾠκοδόμουν·

records.literal_gloss: Likewise as it came to pass in the days of Lot; they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building;

en.L: Likewise, just as it was in the days of Lot: they were eating, they were drinking, they were buying, they were selling, they were planting, they were building;
en.B: It was the same in Lot's time. People ate and drank, bought and sold, planted and built.
en.R: It was the same in the time of Lot. People were eating and drinking. They were buying and selling. They were planting crops and building houses.

fr.L: De même, comme il en a été aux jours de Lot : ils mangeaient, ils buvaient, ils achetaient, ils vendaient, ils plantaient, ils bâtissaient ;
fr.B: Il en a été de même au temps de Lot. Les gens mangeaient et buvaient, achetaient et vendaient, plantaient et construisaient.
fr.R: C’était la même chose au temps de Lot. Les gens mangeaient et buvaient. Ils achetaient et vendaient. Ils plantaient dans leurs champs et construisaient des maisons.

decisions.choice: the days of Lot: the time before Sodom was destroyed
decisions.reason: Genesis 19 tells how Lot, Abraham's nephew, lived in Sodom and was led out before the city was destroyed.

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off: the list is not followed by "so it will be"
decisions.reason: Jesus starts a comparison, lists what people were doing, and goes on in 17:29-30 without finishing the "just as" in the usual way.

decisions.choice: crops ... houses
decisions.reason: Readable says what was planted and built.

source.text: ᾗ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ἐξῆλθεν Λὼτ ἀπὸ Σοδόμων, ἔβρεξεν πῦρ καὶ θεῖον ἀπ’ οὐρανοῦ καὶ ἀπώλεσεν πάντας.

records.literal_gloss: in which then day went out Lot from Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed all.

en.L: But on the day Lot went out from Sodom, it rained fire and sulfur from heaven and destroyed [them] all.
en.B: Then came the day Lot walked out of Sodom. Fire and sulfur fell like rain from heaven, and every one of them was destroyed.
en.R: But on the day Lot left the city of Sodom, fire and burning sulfur came down from the sky like rain. It killed them all.

fr.L: Mais le jour où Lot est sorti de Sodome, il a plu du ciel du feu et du soufre, et [cela] les a tous fait périr.
fr.B: Puis est venu le jour où Lot est sorti de Sodome. Le feu et le soufre sont tombés du ciel comme une pluie, et tous ont péri.
fr.R: Mais le jour où Lot a quitté la ville de Sodome, du feu et du soufre brûlant sont tombés du ciel comme de la pluie. Le feu les a tous tués.

decisions.choice: it rained fire and sulfur from heaven
decisions.reason: The words follow Genesis 19:24, where the LORD rained burning sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah.

decisions.choice: sulfur: the yellow mineral that burns with choking fumes
alternatives: brimstone as a name for hell
decisions.reason: The old word "brimstone" means burning stone, sulfur.

decisions.choice: it rained: God sent it
decisions.reason: The verb has no subject named, but Genesis 19:24 says the LORD sent it.

decisions.choice: from the sky
decisions.reason: The word means the sky and heaven. Readable uses "sky" for the picture of rain.

source.text: κατὰ τὰ αὐτὰ ἔσται ᾗ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἀποκαλύπτεται.

records.literal_gloss: According to these things will it be in which day the Son of Man is revealed.

en.L: It will be just the same on the day the Son of Man is revealed.
en.B: That is how it will be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.
en.R: It will be like that on the day the Son of Man appears.

fr.L: Il en sera de même le jour où le Fils de l’homme est révélé.
fr.B: C’est ainsi qu’il en sera le jour où le Fils de l’homme sera révélé.
fr.R: Ce sera comme cela le jour où le Fils de l’homme apparaîtra.

decisions.choice: is revealed: is shown openly for who he is
decisions.reason: The verb means to uncover. The Son of Man, now hidden, will be seen by all in his glory (2 Thessalonians 1:7).

decisions.choice: appears
decisions.reason: Readable uses a simpler word.

source.text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὃς ἔσται ἐπὶ τοῦ δώματος καὶ τὰ σκεύη αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ, μὴ καταβάτω ἆραι αὐτά, καὶ ὁ ἐν ἀγρῷ ὁμοίως μὴ ἐπιστρεψάτω εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω.

records.literal_gloss: In that day who will be on the housetop and the goods of him in the house, not let him come down to take them away, and the [one] in [the] field likewise not let him return to the things behind.

en.L: In that day, whoever is on the housetop, with {{gender:their|his}} goods in the house, must not come down to take them away; and likewise whoever is in [the] field must not turn back to the things behind.
en.B: On that day anyone up on the roof must not go down into the house to get {{gender:their|his}} things. In the same way, anyone out in the field must not turn around to fetch what is behind.
en.R: On that day, a person who is up on the roof must not go down to get {{gender:their|his}} things from the house. A person out in the field must not go back home for anything.

fr.L: En ce jour-là, celui qui sera sur le toit, et ses affaires dans la maison, qu’il ne descende pas pour les emporter ; et de même celui qui [sera] aux champs, qu’il ne retourne pas vers ce qui est derrière.
fr.B: Ce jour-là, celui qui sera sur le toit ne devra pas descendre dans la maison pour prendre ses affaires. De même, celui qui sera dans les champs ne devra pas faire demi-tour pour aller chercher ce qu’il a laissé derrière lui.
fr.R: Ce jour-là, si quelqu’un est sur le toit, il ne doit pas descendre pour prendre ses affaires dans la maison. Et si quelqu’un est dans les champs, il ne doit pas rentrer chez lui pour chercher quoi que ce soit.

decisions.choice: the housetop: the flat roof of a house, reached by an outside stair
decisions.reason: Roofs were flat and used for work and rest. A person could come down the outside stair and flee without going into the house.

decisions.choice: do not go back for anything: when that day comes, nothing must hold a person back
alternatives: advice on how to escape a disaster
decisions.reason: Jesus uses the picture of a sudden escape to say that a person's whole heart must be ready for him, as the next verse about Lot's wife shows.

decisions.choice: things
decisions.reason: The word means a person's belongings; Balanced and Readable use a common word.

source.text: μνημονεύετε τῆς γυναικὸς Λώτ.

records.literal_gloss: Remember the wife of Lot.

en.L: Remember the wife of Lot.
en.B: Remember Lot's wife.
en.R: Remember what happened to Lot's wife.

fr.L: Souvenez-vous de la femme de Lot.
fr.B: Rappelez-vous la femme de Lot.
fr.R: Souvenez-vous de ce qui est arrivé à la femme de Lot.

decisions.choice: Lot's wife: she looked back as Sodom was destroyed, and became a pillar of salt
decisions.reason: Genesis 19:17, 26. She had been told not to look back. Her looking back showed that her heart was still in the city.

decisions.choice: what happened to
decisions.reason: Readable points the reader to the story.

source.text: ὃς ἐὰν ζητήσῃ τὴν ψυχὴν αὐτοῦ περιποιήσασθαι ἀπολέσει αὐτήν, ὃς δ’ ἂν ἀπολέσῃ ζῳογονήσει αὐτήν.

records.literal_gloss: Whoever if may seek the life of him to save will lose it, whoever but will lose [it] will preserve it.

en.L: Whoever seeks to keep {{gender:their|his}} life will lose it, but whoever loses [it] will preserve it alive.
en.B: Anyone who tries to hold on to {{gender:their|his}} life will lose it, and anyone who loses it will keep it alive.
en.R: Whoever tries to keep {{gender:their|his}} life safe will lose it. But whoever loses it will be kept alive.

fr.L: Celui qui cherchera à conserver sa vie la perdra, et celui qui [la] perdra la gardera vivante.
fr.B: Celui qui essaie de s’accrocher à sa vie la perdra, et celui qui la perd la conservera en vie.
fr.R: Celui qui veut protéger sa vie la perdra. Mais celui qui la perd sera gardé en vie.

decisions.choice: life: the self, the whole person and life itself
alternatives: the soul as distinct from the body
decisions.reason: As in 9:24, holding on to life now means losing life with God.

decisions.choice: keep: gain or keep for oneself
decisions.reason: This is not the usual verb for saving. It means to keep or gain something for oneself (Acts 20:28).

decisions.choice: preserve alive: keep alive, give life to
decisions.reason: The verb means to keep alive (Acts 7:19). The one who lets go of life for Jesus will be given life by God.

decisions.choice: will be kept alive
decisions.reason: Readable uses a passive that points to God as the one who keeps the person alive.

source.text: λέγω ὑμῖν, ταύτῃ τῇ νυκτὶ ἔσονται δύο ἐπὶ κλίνης μιᾶς, ὁ εἷς παραλημφθήσεται καὶ ὁ ἕτερος ἀφεθήσεται·

records.literal_gloss: I say to you, in that night there will be two upon bed one, the one will be taken and the other will be left;

en.L: I tell you, in that night there will be two [people] on one bed; the one will be taken and the other will be left.
en.B: I tell you, that night two people will be sleeping in one bed. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind.
en.R: I tell you, on that night two people will be asleep in the same bed. One of them will be taken. The other will be left.

fr.L: Je vous le dis, cette nuit-là, il y aura deux [personnes] sur un seul lit : l’un sera pris et l’autre sera laissé.
fr.B: Je vous le dis, cette nuit-là, deux personnes dormiront dans le même lit : l’une sera prise, et l’autre laissée.
fr.R: Je vous le dis : cette nuit-là, deux personnes seront endormies dans le même lit. L’une sera prise. L’autre sera laissée.

decisions.choice: taken ... left: one is taken to be with the Lord, the other left behind for judgment
alternatives: taken away in judgment, the other spared
decisions.reason: The words are not explained. "Taken" is used of receiving someone to be with oneself (John 14:3), which points to being gathered to the Lord. But in the flood and at Sodom (17:27, 29) people were taken away by judgment, and some read the picture that way. Either way, two people side by side meet different ends.

decisions.choice: in that night: at the time of the Son of Man's coming
decisions.reason: Jesus pictures people asleep at night and working by day (17:35); the coming may be at any hour.

decisions.choice: two: two people
decisions.reason: The Greek uses the masculine form for a pair, which may include a man and a woman.

decisions.choice: two people ... sleeping (B); asleep (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who is in the bed and what they are doing.

source.text: ἔσονται δύο ἀλήθουσαι ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτό, ἡ μία παραλημφθήσεται ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα ἀφεθήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: There will be two grinding at the same [place], the one will be taken and the other will be left.

en.L: There will be two [women] grinding at the same [place]; the one will be taken and the other will be left."
en.B: Two women will be grinding grain together. One will be taken, and the other will be left behind."
en.R: Two women will be grinding grain together. One of them will be taken. The other will be left."

fr.L: Deux [femmes] moudront au même [endroit] : l’une sera prise et l’autre sera laissée. »
fr.B: Deux femmes moudront du grain ensemble : l’une sera prise, et l’autre laissée. »
fr.R: Deux femmes seront en train de moudre du grain ensemble. L’une sera prise. L’autre sera laissée. »

decisions.choice: two women grinding: two women working one hand mill together
decisions.reason: Grinding grain for the day's bread was women's work, often done by two women turning the upper stone of a hand mill together.

decisions.choice: no verse 36
alternatives: adding verse 36: two men will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts, Codex Bezae among them, and some early translations add a verse like Matthew 24:40 about two men in a field. The oldest Greek manuscripts, including Papyrus 75, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus, do not have it, and it is probably copied from Matthew. The SBLGNT leaves it out, so there is no verse 36 here. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: grinding grain
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was ground.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here
decisions.reason: The disciples ask a question in 17:37.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθέντες λέγουσιν αὐτῷ· Ποῦ, κύριε;

records.literal_gloss: And answering they say to him, Where, Lord?

en.L: And answering, they say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where, Lord?"
en.B: They asked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Where will this happen, Lord?"
en.R: The disciples asked, "Lord, where will this happen?"

fr.L: Et, répondant, ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} disent : « Où, Seigneur ? »
fr.B: Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demandèrent : « Où cela arrivera-t-il, Seigneur ? »
fr.R: Les disciples ont demandé : « Seigneur, où est-ce que cela va arriver ? »

decisions.choice: where: where will these people be taken, or where will this happen
decisions.reason: The question is short and could ask either. Jesus' answer does not give a place.

decisions.choice: they say: a present tense in a story about the past
decisions.reason: Greek storytellers used the present tense to make a scene vivid.

decisions.choice: will this happen
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable complete the short question.

decisions.choice: asked
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use the past tense of the story.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Ὅπου τὸ σῶμα, ἐκεῖ καὶ οἱ ἀετοὶ ἐπισυναχθήσονται.

records.literal_gloss: And he said to them, Where the body [is], there also the vultures will be gathered together.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Where the body [is], there also the vultures will be gathered together."
en.B: He said to them, "Where the corpse lies, there the vultures will flock together."
en.R: Jesus answered, "The vultures come together wherever the dead body is."

fr.L: Et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Là où [est] le corps, là aussi se rassembleront les vautours. »
fr.B: Il leur dit : « Là où gît le cadavre, là s’assembleront les vautours. »
fr.R: Jésus a répondu : « Les vautours se rassemblent partout où il y a un cadavre. »

decisions.choice: where the body is, the vultures gather: a proverb meaning it will be plain to see and cannot be escaped
alternatives: a statement about where the judgment will take place on a map
decisions.reason: Birds circling in the sky show from far off where a dead animal lies. Jesus does not name a place; when the time comes, it will be as plain as that, and judgment will come where it is due (compare Matthew 24:28).

decisions.choice: vultures: birds that feed on dead bodies
decisions.reason: The word can mean eagle or vulture. Birds gathering at a dead body are vultures.

decisions.choice: body: here a dead body
decisions.reason: The word means body; with the birds it means a dead one.

decisions.choice: corpse (B); dead body (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear the body is dead.
